Offline rule-family comparison on held-out mechanics P_hat (24 dev+val snapshots, 849 release rows). Model-selection conclusion: on current data there is no evidence to adopt a form more complex than linear Q - lambda*P_hat. P_hat is decile-calibrated; within the compared range no nonlinear rule beat linear (this removes the miscalibration motivation for nonlinearity but not others: candidate-dependent loss, rotation-magnitude-dependent damage, nonlinear risk tolerance, coarse label proxy, score not being a utility). All families reached 0 selected topples (baseline only 3/24, so 3->0 and 0.005-level loss differences are unstable; family micro-ranking unreadable). Linear-lambda and hard-epsilon sweeps traced nearly the same empirical frontier on these snapshots/candidate sets/grids -- an observation, not a duality theorem (discrete candidate sets can have unsupported Pareto points). hard+fallback never starved offline, which does not rehabilitate the old static enforce gate nor rule out online starvation (live candidate generation differs). State-dependent lambda(s) untestable: remaining items spans 25-34 (scale 0.83-1.13) and is itself an unverified proxy for V_safe - V_fail; early snapshots would be added to identify whether failure loss varies with state.

entries.claim: The official not_placed_safe judgment is close to a step function of settle angle: every band >= 45 deg is unconditionally unsafe (rate 1.000), 30-45 deg is mixed (0.375), and below 30 deg the rate is small (0.073) and displacement-driven (median 0.43 m among unsafe vs 0.06 m among safe). A smooth rotation-magnitude damage model therefore has little room -- one of the listed motivations for a nonlinear risk penalty is measured to be weak. rotated_over_30 is a slightly conservative but structurally faithful proxy for the angle channel; the residual loss mass below the threshold is the unresolved slide channel (d_xy). Exploratory scope: all non-holdout release rows (1121), not frozen-split metrics.

Per-config: 4 of 5 configs improved or tied on placed under every lambda; fill improved even at equal placed (b000-k15: 14 placed both arms, fill 7.27 -> 15.39). Every episode still ends by an unsafe placement -- the risk term delays the topple, it does not eliminate it. Caveats: n=1 per (config, arm) at lambda 1/4; b000 episodes are deterministic under fixed timing while b001 episodes show timing nondeterminism with baseline variance up to 4 placed (b001-k20 off: 13 vs 17), so single-config differences of 1-3 are inconclusive there; the aggregate direction across configs and lambdas is the finding. Round 1 was invalidated by a stale simulator agent copy on both arms (instrument note in run_risk_ablation.py).

Slide direction is predictable from the pre-release contact state: on 422 release rows with |d_xy| > 5 cm, the mean cosine between the observed horizontal displacement and the CoM-offset-from-support-centroid direction is 0.651; 87.4% slide 'downhill' (cos > 0) and 76.3% have cos > 0.5. The long-unresolved d_xy channel was attacked with invariant scalars that discard direction; an equivariant formulation (predict in the local support frame, mirror symmetry by construction) is the indicated fix. Ladder: S0 equivariant baseline without new losses -> S1 learned local-geometry encoder with invariance loss -> S2 test fixed SketchGeo vs Gated Iota on the frozen worst-group extrapolation metrics (user's loss-function document, 2026-07-31).

entries.claim: The d_xy channel yields to the equivariant local-frame formulation (S0, no learned representation): LOSO Spearman |d_xy| 0.282 -> 0.567, signed longitudinal 0.641, large-slide AUC 0.718 -> 0.787, and worst-side extrapolation 0.037 -> 0.399 (better on 6 of 7 sides; only the easy k10 side favours the invariant baseline). Mirror-symmetry prediction confirmed label-side: mean |transverse| 0.039 m vs |longitudinal| 0.085 m. Direction is carried by the zero-parameter downhill prior (0.856); the model's contribution is magnitude and extrapolation stability. Features: com_offset, downhill/uphill margins to the support hull, mechanics scalars, friction/mass/density/is_soft. S1 (learned local-geometry encoder + invariance loss) and S2 (SketchGeo vs Gated Iota on worst-group metrics) remain open as the next rungs.

Post-mortem of 57 episode-ending placements (all ablation episodes; container rebuilt from observed settle AABBs, frozen mech P_rot on the commanded pose): death channels are topple 28, transport_invalid 21, slide 8. Within topples the rotation model mostly saw it coming -- KNOWN (P_rot>=0.5) 6, AMBIGUOUS (0.2-0.5) 17, MISSED (<0.2) only 5 -- so the topple-channel remainder is starvation / insufficient endgame penalty (a state-dependent lambda argument), not perception. The largest untapped lever is the transport_invalid channel (37% of deaths, untouchable by any release-risk lambda): episodes die on transport validation before physics, pointing back at candidate generation / anchor recall in endgame states.

First slide online ablation (5 dev configs, base vs slide lambda 0.5 / 1.0 on top of rot-only lambda=1): slide lambda trades placed for slide-death reduction -- lambda=1.0 cut low-angle unsafe endings 4 -> 1 but cost 4.4 placed per episode (18.4 -> 14.0); lambda=0.5 gained fill (+2.0) at -1.8 placed with slide deaths unchanged. Under the official cutoff gate (placed count gates all non-fill scores) this trade is rejected: RELEASE_RISK_SLIDE_LAMBDA stays 0 in the live default. Slide shadow produced zero changed single selections (4 steps) -- the slide term acts through cumulative trajectory divergence, not single-step swaps. The frozen slide model (slide-dev-v1-20260731) remains available; revisit after S1 improves the estimator or with smaller lambda once the transport channel is fixed.

Candidate supply is NOT the endgame constraint: at all 27 late replay snapshots (steps 11-16, dev+val), the HT-estimated population of official-transport-valid candidates is in the thousands (minimum ~1038, typically 10k-36k), physically placeable-safe candidates are also in the thousands (never zero), and the minimum frozen-mech P_rot among valid sampled candidates is 0.003-0.101. Per the terminal-failure trichotomy: transport_invalid deaths (21) mean the anytime search failed to find/execute any of thousands of valid candidates within budget (recall failure, plausibly the 8 s timeout -> forced random action), and topple deaths mean risky candidates were chosen while near-zero-risk options existed (selection/recall, not perception, and not candidate starvation). Caveat: measured on replay snapshots near-terminal, not the exact dying states of the ablation episodes.

entries.claim: The packed-AABB cache (6.4x candidate throughput) produced a MIXED regression-guard result: b000-k40 +10 placed (11->21, fill 14->27 -- search starvation was binding there) and b000-k15 +1, but b000-k20 -12 (26->14) and b001-k20 -6; net placed 92->84 across the 5 dev configs. Interpretation: higher recall changes every selection, and with the known-defective utility (Ranker volume dead vote, q+gamma*q lookahead) a larger candidate pool can select worse trajectories -- the starved search was acting as an accidental regularizer. The cache is kept (the 78%-waste defect is real and the starvation mechanism is not a defensible control), which promotes selection quality under enlarged candidate sets (Ranker/lookahead) from deferred to blocking. Guard episodes are single trajectories; b001 configs carry timing nondeterminism, but the b000-k20 drop is deterministic-environment real.

entries.claim: The three lookahead selection modes remain essentially degenerate even under the 6.4x-richer search: weighted and depth2 produced identical episodes on all 5 dev configs (84 placed total), pool_resilience differed only on b000-k20 (12 vs 14 placed) and b001-k30 fill, net slightly worse (82). The slide-lambda-not-adopted-v1 verdict was measured on the starved search; under rich search slide becomes the leading uncontrolled hazard, so the slide ablation is being re-run under the cached search before that verdict stands.

First official-evaluation calibration pair. OLD submission (pre-risk era): fill 14.41, num_placed 0.201, cog/stability/placement/soft ALL ZERO, status stopped-in-middle. NEW submission (current risk line: rot lambda=1 mech + slide lambda=0.5 + AABB cache, with minor uncommitted Codex tweaks of unknown diff): fill 27.90, num_placed 0.405, cog 9.60, stability 12.68, placement 2.25, soft 5.00, optimization 150.0 s, policy mean 6.53 s, status still stopped-in-middle (final action failed is_placed_safe/is_valid/is_included). Reads: (1) the placed-count cutoff sits between num_placed 0.201 and 0.405 on this scenario -- crossing it unlocked every component, confirming the gate structure; (2) official fill and placed roughly doubled, matching the local dev-suite direction (+35% placed / +71% fill); (3) policy mean 6.53 s matches POLICY_BUDGET_SECONDS=6.5 exactly -- no timeout margin problem; optimization 150 s is the internal offline budget, inside the 180 s limit; (4) episodes still end by a failed action, so terminal-survival remains the top lever officially too. Component scales/weights remain unknown (single scenario, units unpublished).

entries.claim: Under the current shipped policy (rich search + rot lambda=1 + slide lambda=0.5), transport_invalid is the LEADING death channel: 10/22 episode endings (45%), vs topple 8 (36%) and slide 4 (18%). In the pre-cache era the split was topple 48% / transport 38% / slide 14%. Controlling rotation and slide raised the transport channel's relative share -- the Route-Survival Lookahead (corridor-preservation tie-break, Codex branch) targets the current largest channel. Its success metric: reduce transport_invalid endings on the 7-case suite without net placed loss.

The transport_invalid death channel (45% of current-policy endings) is NOT corridor blocking: all 8 audited fatal actions fail the agent's OWN static_geometry check on the reconstructed state, because they are the unsafe_protocol_fallback -- a fixed-coordinate action (pool item 0 at [0.0, 0.0, 0.25], orientation 0) emitted when the anytime search returns no acceptable candidate. In congested late states that coordinate is occupied/invalid, so the fallback is a poison pill that ends the episode, while thousands of transport-valid candidates exist elsewhere (late-snapshots-not-starved). Consistent with Codex's route_lost=0: routes are geometrically open; the agent gives up and self-destructs. Fix direction: replace the fixed-coordinate fallback with a rescue scan (coarse stride over release anchors across pool item classes, accept the first self-valid candidate), plus stride coverage in the main scan so the no-candidate branch fires less.
entries.source: agent.py unsafe_protocol_fallback (fixed_coordinate); audit of 8 transport-death fatal actions vs Geometry.rejection_reason on rebuilt states

entries.claim: A terminal deadline-reserved rescue scan is rejected in its current form. The breadth-first class/item release scan recovered a statically validated candidate on 37/37 checked-in late snapshots (17/17 case-001), but physical ablations regressed overall: the 0.9 s reserve produced base/rescue totals 83/75 placed and 100.32/86.98 fill; the 0.2 s reserve produced 80/74 and 98.00/88.02. A third trace-enabled run produced 82/78 and 100.32/94.25. In that diagnostic run b001-k20 and b001-k30 each triggered rescue once, but rescue_action_count stayed 0 and the unsafe protocol fallback still fired once; b000-k20 regressed by two placements despite rescue_trigger_count=0. Therefore the late rescue neither replaced the poison fallback nor justified stealing time from the primary search. Keep it default OFF. The next falsifiable design is to include one release unit per item in the primary first pass so a validated incumbent exists before the deadline, without a terminal reserve.

The first cross-step incumbent design (top 2 accepted candidates per stable item and per settled/release kind, shadow only) is rejected as a replacement for unsafe_protocol_fallback. In the 5-config development ablation it retained 1,603 candidates across 76 decisions; every retained item's identity remained visible, but only 702 candidates (43.793%) passed the complete next-state static contract. Revalidation cost 2.864 s total / 37.684 ms per observed step, max 145 ms, with one deadline overrun. The only protocol fallback occurred in b001-k30 in both arms. At the shadow fatal step 16, all 18 retained candidates still had visible items but zero remained valid (17 corridor, 1 static_geometry); validation began 27.8 ms after the internal deadline. would_prevent_protocol_fallback was 0/1. Keep mode default OFF and do not add enforce. Scope: this rejects score-top2 carryover as the fallback guarantee, not diverse carryover as a warm start; general-step survival was nonzero but did not cover the fatal state.
entries.source: reports/cross-step-incumbent/history/30707120494/summary.json; Actions run 30707120494; b001-k30 shadow policy trace artifact

entries.claim: A bounded graded visible-pool rollout separates the known b000-k20 step-9 Ranker divergence where raw next-candidate counts were 2712 vs 1140. Across fixed per-step attempt budgets 64, 128, 256 and 512, the historically successful item-17 action retained one additional settled placement (item 28, 0.08 m3) while the item-28 action retained zero before the static rollout reached an uncertain release transition; the lexicographic rollout therefore ranks item 17 above item 28 at every tested budget. After isolating shadow from the production Z-interval cache, Linux run 30708961145 observed 79 shadow decisions: 39/79 (49.4%) had more than one rollout value and 17/79 (21.5%) proposed a different item; cost was 102.8 ms/step average, 398.3 ms max. Shadow remained telemetry-only. Its single-run placed/fill means were +0.4/+0.674 vs separately executed base, but base itself moved 16.2 -> 14.6 placed between the two screening runs, so this is runner/trajectory variance, not adoption evidence. Scope: one saved divergence plus one 5-config screening run, static settled proxy for the commanded release, no PyBullet candidate counterfactual and no enforce test.

The first graded visible-pool rollout remains a useful discriminator but is rejected as a live ordering in its current form. In the final 8-configuration x 3-repeat same-run ablation (strictly require V_rollout(proposal) > V_rollout(selected), Q_live loss <= 0.15), enforce changed 54/406 decisions and regressed the 8-case mean totals from placed 137.667 / fill 167.881 to 131.000 / 151.656 (-6.667 / -16.225); the 5 development totals moved 84.000 / 104.239 to 79.333 / 95.233. Effects were heterogeneous: b000-k20 gained +0.666 placed and b000-k40 +2.667, but b000-k15 lost 6.000 in every repeat. Non-degeneracy is early-heavy: 138/240 observations (57.5%) at steps 0-9 versus 2/166 (1.2%) after step 9; mean cost 111.1 ms/step, max 617.6 ms. An earlier implementation also exposed and then fixed two invalid enforcement paths (global non-degeneracy and Q_live tie changes); the strict-improvement run still lost, so the negative verdict is about the rollout value/order itself, not only those bugs. Keep VISIBLE_POOL_ROLLOUT_MODE=off. This does not supersede the positive step-9 signal; it scopes it as a diagnostic/candidate feature rather than an adopted policy. Next evidence should be the deterministic b000-k15 first-divergence counterfactual, not blind band tuning.

entries.claim: The step>=10 visible-pool rollout silence measured in enforce run 30716558143 (2/166 = 1.2% non-degenerate) is substantially a coverage artefact of the anchor scan order, not a saturated container. On the 48 committed replay snapshots (37 at step>=10), only 4/37 late snapshots have no arm reaching any future placement and only 1/37 has no arm discriminating at all. At the shipped setting (stride 1, 64 attempts/step) the rollout reaches a future placement on 8/37; at stride 8 with the same per-step attempt cap it reaches one on 28/37 and is non-degenerate on 33/37. Raising the budget instead of the stride is the weaker instrument: budget-512 spends about 8.4x the attempts and reaches a future placement on only 12/37, with 17 late snapshots reached by stride-8 and not by budget-512 versus 1 the other way. budget-N still scores 36/37 on non-degeneracy because extra attempts reach release candidates whose accumulated P_rot/P_slide break the tie without any reach, so non-degeneracy and future-placement must be read separately. Cost: the per-step cap is identical, total consumed attempts rise 205.8 -> 257.7 mean only because surviving branches take another rollout step; wall clock is +17% mean at stride 4 (108.8 vs 92.6 ms) and about 2.9x at stride 8 (267.3 mean, 654.1 max). Scope: static-proxy rollouts on saved states with a deterministically reconstructed Top-K, not a replay of any deadline-limited live search and not a PyBullet counterfactual. This run does not reproduce the live 57.5%/1.2% early/late split (its early band is steps 8-9 only, baseline 2/11); the valid comparison is across arms within a band. This is a diagnosis of the measurement, not adoption evidence: VISIBLE_POOL_ROLLOUT_MODE stays off and VISIBLE_POOL_ROLLOUT_STRIDE defaults to 1.

entries.claim: The deterministic b000-k15 enforce loss from run 30716558143 is caused by the rollout going blind after the divergence it caused, not by the divergent action itself. Local physical re-run (PyBullet 3.2.7, 3 repeats/arm, b000-k15 only): base 17.000 placed / 23.119 fill (bit-identical x3), rollout_enforce 11.000 / 13.228 (bit-identical x3, reproducing the reported -6.000 exactly), and rollout_enforce_stride4 20.333 / 26.018 (20/20/21) -- +3.333 placed and +2.899 fill over base, +9.333 over enforce. Both enforce arms take the SAME first divergence at step 3 (item 12 -> item 3), so the stride does not avoid a bad first action. The difference is afterwards: at stride 1 the episode contains exactly one enforcement and step>=10 non-degeneracy is 0/2, while at stride 4 there are four enforcements (steps 3, 5, 8, 13) and step>=10 non-degeneracy is 5/10. That live 0/2 -> 5/10 confirms the scan-order hole inside the running policy, not only on saved snapshots. Cost per decision rises 77.1/184.7 to 176.0/278.8 ms mean/max; the maximum is below the 617.6 ms the enforce ablation already tolerated. rollout_enforce_stride4 ends on unsafe_protocol_fallback (is_valid false) after surviving nine more steps, a different termination channel from the settle topple ending the other two arms. Scope: ONE configuration, one machine. This explains the b000-k15 loss; it does not revisit the enforce rejection, which was made on eight configurations. VISIBLE_POOL_ROLLOUT_MODE stays off and VISIBLE_POOL_ROLLOUT_STRIDE stays 1 until the eight-configuration repeated ablation at stride 4 plus the reports/benchmarks/baseline.json regression guard have run.

entries.claim: A saved-snapshot sweep can answer 'would the decision at this state change', never 'would the episode outcome change'. Saved snapshots are drawn from one trajectory (here, base); as soon as an arm diverges, the states it actually visits are absent from the snapshot set. This was not hypothetical: the offline b000-k15 sweep found the enforce decision stride-invariant at the sampled steps and was read as evidence that stride would not change the outcome, while the physical re-run moved placed from 11.000 to 20.333. Both readings were correct about their own question. Use offline sweeps to diagnose an instrument; use a physical run to decide an outcome.

Reordering the live anchor scan into stride-interleaved order is rejected as an unconditional default. LIVE_SEARCH_INTERLEAVE stays 1. Local screening (PyBullet 3.2.7, 1 repeat/cell, 5 development configs, base vs live_interleave4): totals placed 83 -> 80 and fill 104.742 -> 91.995. The per-config split is the finding, not the total: b000-k40 +5 placed / +6.078 fill, b000-k15 -3 / -10.464, b000-k20 -4 / -4.483, b001-k20 -1 / -1.281, b001-k30 0 / -2.597. The single winner is the configuration aabb-cache-guard-mixed already identifies as search-starved, and it is the same config that gained +10 from the packed-AABB cache while b000-k20 lost 12. Two independent coverage interventions -- one enlarging the candidate set, one only permuting its scan order -- now produce the same per-configuration signature. Search diagnostics exclude reduced recall as the cause: both arms are deadline-limited on most steps, the unit completion ratio does not fall (b000-k15 0.285 -> 0.330), and no episode ended in a no-candidate branch the base arm avoided; what changed is which candidate a truncated search settles on and hence which trajectory is taken. This is the second measurement establishing that selection quality is blocking for coverage work, not the reverse. Scope: one repeat per cell, and the two smallest deltas are on the timing-nondeterministic b001 cases. Local base totals (83 / 104.742) are BELOW the registered development baseline (88 / 114.6) because the search is deadline-limited and absolute totals are machine-dependent -- only base-vs-arm within one run is comparable, which matters most for a change whose entire effect is about what a deadline truncates. This does not retract the scan-order coverage hole, which remains measured and real; the b000-k40 gain is that hole being closed where closing it helps. A targeted form (interleave only when the search is starving) is a different design and is untested. [2026-08-02 DOWNGRADED: development-suite-noise-floor-permutation measured base placed sd 2.315 and range 7 across permutations of one multiset. Every per-config delta in this screening (+5/-4/-3/-1/0) lies inside that band, and the screening was UNPAIRED across streams, so it does not establish a negative. Read as NOT ESTABLISHED. LIVE_SEARCH_INTERLEAVE stays 1 because nothing established a positive either; a paired permutation design would settle it.]

Redefining a residual option from geometrically placeable to placeable-and-likely-to-survive does NOT rescue the acceptance-capacity state value. On 42 development snapshots (3 final_holdout datasets skipped; 17 with an uncensored physical failure), weighting each independent option by modelled survival makes the relation to the physical-failure label worse under every combination rule: Spearman vs T_physical 0.503 (raw) -> 0.251 (union-bound sum), 0.251 (max), 0.214 (independence product); AUC vs Y_3 0.627 -> 0.524 / 0.567 / 0.536. All three rules agree, so this is robust and not an artefact of the combination choice. The motivating diagnosis was also wrong, which strengthens the negative: the constant-class fraction is 0.0 for raw as well as weighted and raw takes 12 distinct totals, so this counting never saturated -- the constant 0.113 in stage-a-calibrated-negative was release_cap_volume, a different quantity. Weighting ADDS resolution (12 -> 37 distinct totals) and LOSES signal. Mechanism: release options are 48.4% of independent options and the models are not degenerate (P_rot mean 0.245 sd 0.135; P_slide mean 0.152 sd 0.144 over 184 class-observations), but the net effect is near a uniform shrink (kappa_product/kappa_raw 0.810 mean, sd 0.110), contributing variation unaligned with the outcome. The structural reason is that an episode fails from the action the policy actually takes, not from the average safety of the option pool, so per-option risk cannot aggregate into a state descriptor for a failure caused by one selected action. Raw kappa's 0.503 must NOT be read as predictive power: Spearman(kappa_raw, step) = -0.367 and Spearman(step, T_physical) = -0.342, so both decline with step and the correlation appears without either informing the other -- the third measurement of the same confound. Conclusion is about form, not weights: the within-state per-action differential is the only shape these confounds do not reach.

entries.claim: Unconditional irreversibility (s not in K => T_a(s) not in K) is FALSE for the rigid option type and holds for priority only in a degenerate way. Over 126 real placements on 42 development states (successors at the official x_plus pose, final_holdout skipped): placing a SOFT item RAISES the rigid independent-option count by +0.261 on average, up in 10 of 23 transitions -- a repeated counterexample, mechanistically soft items settling into gaps and leaving flat top surfaces. Rigid placements also raise their own type in 35/126 (27.8%). By contrast kappa_priority does not move AT ALL under non-priority placements: 0.000 mean with 0 increases and 0 decreases over 57 transitions (19 soft, 38 rigid); only priority placements change it, by the mechanical -1.000 of pool depletion. So the split K = K_irreversible intersect K_recoverable is supported with a MEASURED assignment: rigid is recoverable, soft is eroded by everything (1 increase in 126), priority is invariant. The consequence for a priority hard veto is not the expected one: the risk is not that the set is recoverable and the veto unsound, it is that kappa_priority is constant along ordinary packing, so a veto keyed on it could be sound and never fire. Scope: integer option count at stride 16, cap 32 accepted anchors per class-orientation-kind, so sub-granular movement is invisible; 108 of 126 transitions survived settle and failures are retained.
entries.values: cross-effect mean delta kappa, rows placed / cols measured (diagonal confounded by pool depletion): priority -> (-1.000, -0.500, -1.542) n=24; soft -> (0.000, (-1.174), +0.261) n=23; rigid -> (0.000, -0.076, (+0.025)) n=79

entries.claim: Free space is NOT monotone under placement in this simulator, so any viability argument that assumes 'a placement only adds obstacles and never moves existing ones' needs that premise measured rather than assumed. Tracking already-packed items across a single further placement over 6 consecutive-step snapshot pairs (69 item-observations): 5 (7.2%) moved more than 1 mm, with median displacement 0.028 mm, mean 1.296 mm and MAXIMUM 40.9 mm. The maximum is 2.5x the 16 mm internal boundary guard and transport clearance, so an existing obstacle can leave a fixed corridor or reserved region, which means g(T_a(s)) <= g(s) can be violated for a fixed geometric resource. The distribution is heavy-tailed: most items do not move and a few move a lot. A hard permanent veto therefore needs a margin delta covering the disturbance envelope rather than plain monotonicity. Scope: 6 pairs, 69 observations -- the direction is clear but the envelope value is a first estimate, and denser labelling is cheap now that PyBullet runs locally.
entries.values: 69 already-packed items across one further placement: 5 moved >1 mm (7.2%); displacement median 0.028 mm, mean 1.296 mm, max 40.861 mm vs 16 mm guard

entries.claim: Any dynamic future-class weighting of the form sum_c p(c | h_t) V_c is blocked by data rather than by theory in this repository: simulator/configs/sample_config.json contains exactly two item streams (case 000: 41 items over 10 distinct classes; case 001: 42 items over 9). p(c | h_t) cannot be estimated from two sequences without an exchangeability assumption, and anything learned would be fitting two samples. Task B/C configurations are derived from these same two streams by varying look-ahead, so they do not add independent arrival information.

entries.claim: The within-state per-action kappa differential does NOT predict which sibling survives its settle. On 42 development states with 4 Q-band siblings each (252 pairs, final_holdout skipped), sign agreement between delta kappa and the official is_placed_safe is exactly 0.500 under every weighting: raw 3/6, and 6/12 for each of sum, max and product. This was the test the option-value line was pointing at, run against real validator labels rather than a proxy, and it is null. Combined with stage-a-calibrated-negative (capacity does not explain placed-to-go because episodes end by topple) and risk-weighted-kappa-state-value-negative (weighting by modelled survival made the state descriptor worse), the conclusion is that OPTION SPACE AND PHYSICAL SURVIVAL ARE SEPARATE AXES: no rearrangement of an option count -- absolute, risk-weighted, or per-action differential -- has reached the survival axis. The rollout_placed and rollout_volume agreement of 1.000 (5/5 raw, 7/7 weighted) is NOT validation: both the rollout and kappa are computed from the same realised successor and both count what still fits, so it is an internal consistency check between two capacity measures, not a test against an outcome. Structural byproduct worth its own weight: 240 of 252 sibling pairs (95.2%) had IDENTICAL physical survival and 245 (97.2%) identical rollout placed and volume, with sibling outcomes 154 survivals to 14 failures -- inside a 0.15 Q-band the short-horizon outcome is almost always the same whichever sibling is chosen, which bounds what any within-band reranking can achieve at this horizon regardless of the ranking quantity. Scope: 6 to 12 decided pairs, so this rules out a large effect and not a small one; siblings come from a stratified sample rather than the full population.
entries.values: sign agreement vs is_placed_safe: raw 3/6 = 0.500, sum 6/12 = 0.500, max 6/12 = 0.500, product 6/12 = 0.500; 240/252 pairs (95.2%) outcome-tied

entries.claim: The development suite has a large and previously unmeasured noise floor, and it is NOT reachable by repeats. Running the unchanged shipped agent on 8 PERMUTATIONS of the same 41-item multiset (source case 000, look-ahead 20, arrival order the only thing varied, episodes run sequentially because the search is deadline-limited): placed mean 12.750 with sd 2.315 and range 7 (11 to 18); fill mean 13.593 with sd 3.948 and range 12.547 (9.923 to 22.470). Reordering the same items changes placed by up to 7. Critically, REPEATS DO NOT SAMPLE THIS SOURCE: the same config repeated 3 times is bit-identical (base 17/17/17 and rollout_enforce 11/11/11 on b000-k15), so all prior 3-repeat ablations measured zero of this variance. The whole development suite is five configurations derived from TWO streams by varying look-ahead, so between-stream variation was never estimated. Consequence for prior calls: any UNPAIRED per-configuration delta smaller than about 2 sd is not distinguishable from arrival-order coincidence. The live interleave screening (+5/-4/-3/-1/0 per config, total -3) sits entirely inside this band and its rejection must be downgraded to 'not established' rather than 'measured negative'. Paired within-stream comparisons remain valid and are the design to use. Scope: one source case, one look-ahead, 8 permutations of one multiset; permutation holds content and difficulty fixed and therefore estimates arrival-order variance only, not between-scenario variance.
entries.values: base over 8 permutations: placed mean 12.750 sd 2.315 range 7 (11-18); fill mean 13.593 sd 3.948 range 12.547

entries.claim: Raising the item-dimension cap from the shipped 10 to 16 improves placed on EVERY one of 8 permuted streams: paired mean +3.125 placed (sd 2.800), 8 wins / 0 losses / 0 ties, sign-test p = 0.0039. Fill is weaker and noisier: mean +2.502 (sd 5.359) with 5 wins and 2 losses, so the reliable claim is about placement count, not packing efficiency. This is the first intervention measured here with a consistent sign across independent arrival orders, and it is on the ITEM axis - the one axis where a breadth intervention has ever paid (class-aware coverage moved placed 10.67 -> 17.00), while the anchor axis has now failed twice (aabb cache mixed, live interleave inside the noise band). Mechanism is reach rather than rescue: mean steps 13.75 -> 16.88, deadline-reached rate 82.7% -> 87.4%, and the fallback ending count is unchanged at 1/8 episodes in both arms - the cap does not fix the poison fallback, it simply places more items before the episode ends. Scope: one source case, one look-ahead, 8 permutations of one multiset; the paired design controls arrival order but not item mix, and no timing regression check has been run. [2026-08-02 SUPERSEDED same day: the 8/0/0 was measured on ONE item multiset and does not reproduce on another. See item-cap-effect-is-source-dependent.]

entries.claim: Raising the item cap from 10 to 16 is NOT an unconditional win; the effect depends on the item mix. Paired permutation design, 8 permuted streams per source, look-ahead 20, episodes sequential. Source 000 (41 items, 10 classes, 13 soft, 4 priority): +3.125 placed, 8 wins / 0 losses / 0 ties, two-sided sign test p = 0.0078. Source 001 (42 items, 9 classes, 11 soft, 2 priority): -0.125 placed, 3 wins / 4 losses / 1 tie, p = 1.0 -- nothing. Pooled over both mixes: +1.500 placed, 11 wins / 4 losses / 1 tie, p = 0.1185, NOT established. Keep MAX_POOL_ITEMS_EVALUATED at 10. Candidate mechanism, untested: the cap binds only where the pool is hard to place from. Base placed is 12.750 on source 000 versus 16.625 on source 001, so the shipped cap of 10 may already be sufficient on the easier mix -- which would make this a conditional intervention like the interleave, not a default. Second measurement of the noise floor, on an independent multiset, agrees with the first: source 001 base placed sd 2.722 with range 9 (12 to 21), against source 000 sd 2.315 range 7. Also note the between-source gap in base placed (12.750 vs 16.625, 3.875) exceeds most effects this project chases, so cross-source per-configuration comparisons carry almost no information. On source 000 only, cap 20 gives +5.000 placed (6 wins / 1 loss / 1 tie) but sd 4.781 and cap20-minus-cap16 is +1.875 with 5 wins / 3 losses -- no clean plateau, and not run on source 001.

entries.claim: First long-horizon paired measurement of the shipped utility, and it points the wrong way. On one episode (b000-k20), 6 branch points x 3 siblings from the same candidate set, each branch forced at its step and then run to completion by the shipped policy: within-step concordance between immediate Q and final placed is 0.267 (4 agree / 11 disagree / 1 tie), identical for final fill, against a chance level of 0.500. In 5 of 6 branch points the LOWEST-Q sibling gave the best final placed and fill; at step 4 it reached 24 placed against the control's 14. The obvious confound is refuted: Ranker.score contains 12.0*volume so low Q correlates with small items and placing small items first trivially raises a later count, but placed volume predicts the outcome at only 0.385 (p = 0.58) and at step 8 the winning sibling placed the LARGEST available item at the LOWEST Q. NOT ESTABLISHED: n = 15 decided pairs, two-sided p = 0.1185, one episode of one configuration, and against the measured noise floor (placed sd 2.3) differences like 14 vs 15 are noise while 14 vs 24 is not. Four validity bounds: one branch had a broken prefix and is excluded; one control (step 8) did not reproduce the reference and is one of the steps carrying the effect; the reference itself differed between two runs of this harness (16 steps / fill 17.795 versus 15 / 16.477) because the driver's own capture deep-copies the observation at each branch step and perturbs a deadline-limited search -- the earlier bit-identical 3-repeat result was on the subprocess harness and does not vouch for this one; and step 12 had no control at all because the live policy's action fell outside the offline-reconstructed sibling set. Significance for direction of work: every other negative this session concerned candidate QUANTITY (option counts, risk weighting, scan coverage). This is the first measurement aimed at the ORDERING, and if it holds up then better candidate generation cannot help, because the selector prefers the worse candidate. [2026-08-02 SUPERSEDED same day: the concordance figure thresholded branch differences against a permutation sd, which is a different variance axis and makes that filtering invalid. sigma_branch was then measured directly and is the same size as the effects. One of the two case studies (step 6) reverses under repeats. See sigma-branch-is-the-size-of-the-effects.]
entries.values: within-step concordance, higher Q -> better outcome: placed 4/11/1 = 0.267 (p=0.1185), fill 4/11/1 = 0.267; volume control 5/8/3 = 0.385 (p=0.5811); lowest-Q sibling best in 5 of 6 branch points

entries.claim: Re-running the SAME forced branch from the SAME parent state does not reproduce. Two branch states (b000-k20, steps 4 and 6), 3 siblings each, 3 repeats per branch: placed moves by up to 4 and fill by up to 8.9 within a single branch (step 4 control [21,17,17] fill [28.18,21.90,21.90]; step 6 control [21,21,17] fill [13.04,13.04,21.90]); only 2 of 6 branches were identical across repeats. sigma_branch is therefore the same order as the differences being interpreted, and a single-run branch label carries little information alone. The capture is NOT the cause: harness_perturbs_reference is false, the capturing and capture-free references agreeing within the run, so the nondeterminism is deeper than this driver. Consequence for the earlier claim: the two large-effect case studies are now one. Step 4 survives directionally (control 18.3 -> lowest-Q 25.3, terminal regret 7 placed) though its own control moved from 14 to 17-21 between runs; step 6 REVERSES (control 19.7 -> lowest-Q 19.0, q_argmax_rank_by_outcome = 1, terminal regret 0). Note also that the b000-k15 3-repeat bit-identical result was on the subprocess run_test.py harness and does not extend to episode-level determinism in general. Instrument defect recorded rather than reported as data: forced_action_accepted is false on every branch while episodes run 17-26 steps, so the info key being read is wrong. Next question is causal rather than statistical: averaging repeats shrinks sigma_branch by 1/sqrt(n) at 3-5x cost and only packs the noise down, whereas the cause may be fixable. Suspects in order: the deadline-limited search reacting to wall-clock load; PyBullet state not fully seeded by env.reset(seed=42); allocation or GC timing. Cheap diagnosis: replay one branch three times, persist the chosen action per step, find the first divergent step, and check whether that step's search hit its deadline.
entries.values: within-branch repeat spread: placed up to 4, fill up to 8.9; 2 of 6 branches identical; step 4 terminal regret 7 placed (direction holds), step 6 regret 0 (reversed)

entries.claim: The one improvement case that survived repeats yields no proximate mechanism, and is dropped rather than explained. b000-k20 step 4, winner (lowest Q +0.522) 26 steps / 25 placed / fill 22.349 versus loser (highest Q +0.761) 18 steps / 17 placed / fill 21.896. Predictions were registered in the repository BEFORE the diff was read. H (repairability) was predicted to hold: direction right, mechanism wrong -- the loser does die physically, ending at step 17 with settle angle 88.4 deg and displacement 1.061 m against the winner's worst of 17.3 deg / 0.214 m, but the topple is immediately terminal so the predicted 'irremovable debris then no recovery' phase never happens. Decisively, the branch is at step 4 and the death at step 17, thirteen steps and two entirely different trajectories apart, so this does not support a causal link. R (alternativity) does NOT separate: support components just after the branch are 5/5, 5/5, 6/5, and the ordering reverses later (steps 11 and 12 give the LOSER more, 7 and 8 against 6 and 6); largest_support_area is 2.9000 in both branches at every step because it is the container floor, so that field measured nothing. A (acceptance breadth) is NOT MEASURABLE here and is an instrument defect rather than a result: classes_with_a_settled_option swings between 0/10 and 10/10 on adjacent steps because the probe used stride=16 limit=1 and recorded 'sparse probe found nothing' as 'no class can be placed'. Surviving negative finding worth keeping: whatever the step-4 choice did, it is NOT visible within three steps in support components, largest support area, or class acceptance. The difference lies either in an unmeasured quantity or is not a state property at all but accumulated trajectory divergence -- and since sigma_branch was measured large (the same branch replayed moves placed by up to 4), an 8-placement gap 13 steps downstream may be substantially divergence rather than consequence. No improvement case now remains as a source for a board functional.
entries.values: winner 26 steps / 25 placed / 22.349 fill; loser 18 steps / 17 placed / 21.896 fill, terminal settle 88.4 deg and 1.061 m; support components after the branch 5/5, 5/5, 6/5 with the ordering reversing by step 11

entries.claim: The official feedback for submission22.zip (total 17.58143419644042) shows fill 29.276, cog 14.224, stability 20.721, placement 4.45, soft 7.65, num_placed_items 0.434, status 'Stopped in the middle'. Three things follow. (a) The bundled evaluator computes only fill_score and num_placed_items (simulator/src/ground_handling/evaluator.py:82-85), so four of the six official components have never had a local signal; every measurement in this repository has been on a 2-of-6 projection. (b) Recovering the component weights from this log is not identifiable: on a 0.05 grid of weight vectors summing to 1, 83 of them reproduce 17.58143 to within 0.05, with fill's weight spanning 0.00-0.45. An earlier reading of 'fill about 0.30, stability about 0.25' was an artefact of enumeration order and is RETRACTED. (c) The placed-count cutoff already recorded in docs/COMPETITION_QA.md:9 is quantitatively consistent with the log, but does NOT explain placement and soft. Taking each component on 0-100 and writing observed = f * E[.|pass], stability forces f >= 0.207; at that lower bound E[placement|pass] <= 21.5 and E[soft|pass] <= 36.9, and both bounds fall further as f rises. So conditional on clearing the cutoff, priority and soft placement are still poor, independently of how many items get placed.

The 0-100 scale assumption behind the f >= 0.207 bound is inferred from fill's min(100*x, 100) clamp and the example's soft = 100.0; it is not stated in the rules. The cutoff value itself is undisclosed, and the score weights remain unknown.

entries.claim: Board receptivity (acceptance breadth A, alternativity R, sealed void and roughness H, read off a 2.5D height map) as a top-K selection rule is REPRODUCIBLY MIXED and does not ship. Two paired blocks against a simultaneously-run base arm on the five development configs, LOOKAHEAD_TOP_K held at the shipped 3. Block 1 total +12 placed (84 -> 96), block 2 +4 (86 -> 90); pooled 10 pairs 6W/3L/1T, sign test p = 0.508. The per-config picture is the result, and it is not noise: b000-k40 +4/+5 and b001-k30 +4/+4 are reproducible WINS with both arms stable across repeats; b001-k20 -5/-4 is a reproducible LOSS with base stable at 18/18. The other two configs are unstable rather than neutral -- on b000-k15 the BOARD arm itself swings 23 -> 16 (7 placed, the full known noise range) while base holds 17/17, and on b000-k20 base swings 14 -> 17 while board holds 17/17. So block 1's headline +12 was carried by one unreplicated +6. Net effect is about +4 on a base of 85, inside the suite noise band, with a real counter-mechanism on b001-k20 that is unexplained. Two side results are firm. The topk8 control shows widening K alone does almost nothing: it reproduces base exactly on 3 of 5 configs, and the traces show identical immediate scores with different item indices, so the stream carries interchangeable items -- the board arms' differences are the selection rule, not the wider candidate set. And the board rule is CHEAPER than the shipped weighted mode, returning at 5.03 s where base hits 6.53 s, because it drops the per-candidate deepcopy and re-search.

entries.claim: 46% of development episodes (16 of 35 in reports/board-receptivity) end at unsafe_protocol_fallback with zero candidates. Probing three of those terminal states answers two questions and the answers point in different directions. (a) The agent's stacking rule IS stricter than the official one: support_surfaces() admits a packed item only when it is neither soft nor prioritized, while simulator/README.md:379 explicitly allows soft-on-soft and priority-on-priority. But relaxing to the official rule unlocked ZERO placements at 3 of 3 states, and all three states had restricted surfaces available to unlock (b001-k20 had 7 soft plus 1 priority plus 1 both). The over-constraint is not what causes these fallbacks. (b) A valid placement DID exist at 2 of 3 states, under the shipped rule, and cheaply. On b000-k40 step 18, 256 attempts per item finds placements for 6 of 23 visible items in 1.935 s of pool-wide search; on b001-k30 step 17, 1 of 25 in 1.430 s. The live step had 6.5 s and found none. Its own diagnostics at those steps read units 1/120 completed, deadline_reached true, items_with_candidates 0. entries.claim: The Task A offline order search was barely running. ADR-001 section 5 assumed a slow placement core would simply reduce the evaluation count, but time control was a global deadline only, with no per-item bound: an unplaceable item's candidate scan made a single complete-order dry run cost about 35 s. Measured on the bundled Task A case 000 (41 items) at the official 150 s internal budget, the legacy default evaluated 3.0 of its allowed 1000 complete orders in 3/3 repeats -- the constructive seed plus two neighbours -- and stopped with about 36 s unused because the ADR-001 moving-average guard will not start an evaluation costing more than the remaining time. Neither neighbour improved placed count or first-failure index, so the shipped order beat the seed only on lower-priority lexicographic keys. A 5 s local probe isolated two serial sinks in sequence: bounding items at 64 attempts finished the seed evaluation in 1.82 s, after which pair-macro generation consumed the remaining 3.18 s. Both stages had to be bounded before order search could open up. This closes ADR-001 Remaining Work 5 with a negative answer for the legacy configuration. Scope: the search was starved, not inert -- do not restate this as 'local search was disabled'.

A 64-attempt per-item budget is rejected: more orders, worse orders. Actions run 30717533328 (30 s budget, 3 repeats) confirmed the structural transfer -- evaluated complete orders went from 1 to 58 for source 000 and 1 to 102 for source 001 -- but the evaluator then severely under-estimated the executable prefix. Physical placed moved 20.0 to 19.33 on source 000 and 13.0 to 14.33 on source 001, with lower fill in both. The lesson is that orders-evaluated is not the objective: the product of order count and per-order evaluation depth has to stay inside the budget, and 64 buys breadth by making each evaluation too shallow to rank orders correctly. Do not read this as a rejection of bounding itself; 128 was adopted on the same mechanism.

bounded128 is the adopted Task A shipped default (ADR-002): OFFLINE_DRY_RUN_ATTEMPTS_PER_ITEM=128 and OFFLINE_PAIR_MACRO_BUDGET_SECONDS=0.5. Adoption run 30717998654, bundled case 000, official 150 s internal / 180 s external budgets, 3 repeats per arm: placed 20/20/20 to 25/25/25 (+25%), fill 29.298 to 34.949 (+19.3%), evaluated complete orders 3.0 to 51.3, centre-of-mass height 0.753 to 0.735 m, near-misses 0 in both arms, policy time held at about 6.51 s, optimization 112.1 s to 147.3 s (inside 150 s internal, 180 s external). The adopted arm is deterministic: fill min equals max across all three repeats, so the same order and the same physical outcome every time, while the base arm's fill varied 27.541 to 30.176 on a constant placed count. Scope is Task A only: both constants are read solely by DryRunEvaluator and Agent.optimize, and the official harness calls optimize only when the case sets agent.optimize -- pinned by test_offline_budget_never_reaches_the_online_policy. Measured on one case at two attempt budgets (64 rejected, 128 adopted); 256 and above and an item-count-adaptive budget are unmeasured, and the 2.7 s of remaining internal headroom means any placement-core slowdown costs evaluations here first. Both arms still end with is_valid and is_placed_safe false (base at step 21, adopted at step 26 of 41 items), so this is not a passing episode in either arm -- the adoption moves the terminal invalid action five placements later, it does not remove it. Verified before the default flip by re-running both arms locally on 4 vCPU: the `default` arm, which sets no OFFLINE_* variable, reproduced the CI bounded128 fill 34.94904885879026 exactly and base reproduced the CI base minimum 27.540718986088258, so the shipped path and the forced path agree.

The offline dry-run proxy is a relative order selector, not a calibrated predictor of physical placements, and the sign of its error is not stable. In adoption run 30717998654 the base arm's proxy predicted 21 against 20 physical placements (over by 1) while the adopted arm predicted 23 against 25 (under by 2). It ranked the arms correctly, which is the only property the search needs, since every order is compared against other orders under one fixed evaluator. Never quote a proxy value as a predicted score, a target, or a result; report physical placed and fill.

The Task A adoption reproduced after the default flip, measuring the submission path rather than an environment override. Actions run 30719944050 re-ran the same matrix with a `default` arm that sets no OFFLINE_* variable at all, in place of the forced bounded128 arm: placed 25/25/25, fill mean/min/max all 34.949049; base unchanged at 20/20/20 with its entire fill distribution reproducing run 30717998654 exactly (mean 29.297655, min 27.540719, max 30.176123). Only search-effort counters moved -- evaluated orders 51.3 -> 49.3 adopted and 3.0 -> 3.3 base, optimization 147.3 -> 146.7 s -- and none of them moved an outcome. One base repeat reached 4 evaluated orders and still placed 20, which is additional evidence that the legacy arm is starved rather than unlucky. The adopted result now rests on three independent executions with bit-identical fill: forced arm on CI, shipped default on a local 4-vCPU box, shipped default on CI. Consequence for experiment design on this case: run-to-run variance is not a confounder, unlike the visible-pool screening where the base arm itself moved 16.2 -> 14.6 between runs. This replicates the adoption; it does not extend it to a second case, a different attempt budget, or the terminal-failure channel.

Merging the live trunk (origin/experiment/anchor-recall-oracle, 21 commits) into this branch RESTORES Task A placed 20 -> 25. The change responsible is the trunk's 13381bd, which adopted OFFLINE_DRY_RUN_ATTEMPTS_PER_ITEM = 128 as the Task A default. It was never on this branch, so every submission artefact built here before the merge was missing it. The two adopted defaults INTERACT, because attempt_budget is a total across a scan while ANCHOR_FIRST_PASS_ATTEMPTS is the per-unit round cap. The offline dry run gives each item 128 total attempts; at the old first-pass cap of 64 that explored two units per item, and at 256 it explores one unit deeply. The Task A neutrality check run before the merge (109 -> 119 s, identical placed and fill) therefore does not carry over and was re-run. Re-measured with both defaults present, on the sample Task A case: placed 25 at both first-pass depths; fill 35.760 at 256 against 34.949 at 64; optimization 148.89 s against 148.82 s, both inside the 150 s internal budget and 31 s under the official 180 s limit; policy 6.514 s at both. The new shake proxy shows the same direction as on the development configs: 15 of 25 items shift at 256 against 13 of 25 at 64, peak kinetic energy 13.50 against 10.99. So on Task A the first-pass change is neutral on placed, slightly better on fill, and slightly worse on the stability proxy. Local optimization time 148.89 s also matches the official log's 149.45 s, which independently corroborates that the trunk's offline default is what submission22 ran.

entries.claim: Task A determinism holds for the OFFLINE ORDER ONLY; the episode outcome is machine-speed dependent, so the earlier 'run-to-run variance is not a confounder' inference is withdrawn. Actions run 30721071243 re-ran the adopted arm a third time and returned placed 25.333 [25, 26] with fill mean 35.614555 -- the same arm and code that produced a constant 25 / 34.949049 in runs 30717998654 and 30719944050. Local sweeps on case 000 pin the mechanism: at OFFLINE_MAX_EVALUATIONS of 50, 55, 60 and unlimited the search selects an IDENTICAL 41-element order every time, yet physical placed is 26 when a seed dry run costs 1.26-1.35 s and 25 when it costs 1.93 s on a slower box. policy_seconds saturates at 6.515-6.522 in every run, so the online policy is anytime: a faster machine buys more candidates per step and can place one more item from the same order. Consequences: (1) the offline order search is genuinely deterministic and machine-independent, and that part of the adoption stands; (2) the adopted arm's physical result is a range, 25-26 placed and 34.949-36.946 fill, not a constant; (3) an evaluation-count cap has NO demonstrated effect -- 26 occurs with no cap at all, so the earlier 'capping at 50 gains one placement' read was a confound between cap and box speed. The base arm remained 20/20/20 with fill mean 29.297655 in all three CI runs, so the adoption's direction is unaffected; only its precision is.

entries.claim: The Task A offline evaluator does not apply the release risk rerank, so it simulates a different policy than the one that executes. Agent.policy passes risk_lambda = RELEASE_RISK_RERANK_LAMBDA when RELEASE_RISK_LIVE_RERANK is set, but DryRunEvaluator.evaluate calls PlacementCore.rescue_choose/choose with no risk_lambda, and apply_release_risk returns release scores unchanged when it is None. Verified by ablation: setting RELEASE_RISK_RERANK_LAMBDA to 1.0, to 50.0, and disabling the live rerank all leave the dry-run result bit-identical on the same input. The shipped executor is risk-on (Q - 1.0*P_rot - 0.5*P_slide) while the offline evaluator models the pre-risk greedy policy. ADR-001 section 2 explicitly lists ranking among what the dry run must share with policy(), so this is an undocumented simulation gap rather than a recorded decision. Three consequences: (1) it gives a mechanism for task-a-offline-proxy-is-relative-only -- the proxy's error is partly systematic bias from modelling another policy, not just miscalibration; (2) bounded128 optimises an order for a pre-risk executor which a risk-on executor then runs, so its +5 placed gain is robustness rather than design; (3) risk-model commits (8669efc, 00ddc64, 70a72a4, 2cb450c) did NOT change E_theta, so any list of 'commits that silently changed the offline optimizer' must exclude them. Closing the gap and leaving it open both require re-measuring Task A: closing it moves E_theta, leaving it open needs an ADR that states the split deliberately.

entries.claim: Task A is a two-stage search and the offline/online ranking split is now a recorded decision (ADR-003), not a defect. The measured fact is unchanged: Agent.policy passes risk_lambda while DryRunEvaluator.evaluate does not, and ablating RELEASE_RISK_RERANK_LAMBDA to 1.0, 50.0 or off leaves the dry-run result bit-identical, so the offline evaluator ranks risk-off while the shipped executor is risk-on. What changes is the reading. DryRunEvaluator is not a faithful simulator of production; it is a cheap, deterministic proposal oracle whose job is to hand promising orders to the real risk-on agent and the official physics for final judgement. Its requirements are relative discrimination between orders, machine independence (ADR-002), and not losing good orders -- not agreement with the live ranker. E_proposal != E_execution is therefore permitted, and the only failure mode that matters is the proposal oracle dropping good candidates. ADR-001 section 2 was amended to share feasibility semantics only (inclusion, collision, support, orientation/anchor construction, transition proxy, invalid judgement); enumeration budget, deadline rule, rescue and ranking/risk may differ. This entry withdraws the previous claim that the gap gives a systematic-bias explanation for the proxy error: the policy difference is one CANDIDATE cause of proxy 23 versus physical 25-26, and neither the sign nor the magnitude of that gap is explained. A risk-on dry run is not rejected -- it is retained as a future comparison arm, and running it would move E_theta and stale every Task A number, so it must be designed as an experiment.

entries.claim: The online item cap is a hard-coded constant that has never been varied, and its cost is unobserved rather than merely unmeasured. MAX_POOL_ITEMS_EVALUATED = 10 sits at agent/agent.py:100 with no environment override, so at pool 40 the agent evaluates 25% of the visible items and no experiment on the cap has ever been possible. No existing instrument can price the exclusion: the replay dataset emits one row per candidate of a SELECTED item, and measure_anchor_recall.py applies the cap before enumerating (lines 379, 391), so its recall figures are conditioned on the ten items the cap admitted. An item that never entered the search has nothing computed about it, so its opportunity cost cannot be recovered from any log -- answering this requires a paired cap sweep or shadow evaluation of skipped items, i.e. a new intervention. The reason to expect it matters: merely REALLOCATING the same ten slots (class-aware coverage) moved pool-40 placed 10.67 -> 17.00 with priority C1 0% -> 81.2%, the largest single effect in this ledger, and that was achieved without touching the cap. Structural reading: the item axis carries 1 knob and 1 ledger entry while candidate_rank carries 4 knobs and 8, so the imbalance reflects which axes had knobs, not which axes mattered. The absence of a knob is why the hypothesis was never formed.

entries.claim: The stability worry raised against ANCHOR_FIRST_PASS_ATTEMPTS = 256 does NOT replicate, and the change is confirmed a third time. Ten paired episodes (five development configs, two blocks) of the shipped default against first_pass64, read on placed, fill and the new local proxies. 64 minus 256: placed -2.70 (1W/8L/1T, p = 0.0391), fill -2.95 (1W/9L, p = 0.0215). On stability the direction REVERSES against the n = 1 reading that prompted this run: the shifted fraction, normalised by item count so an arm that places more items does not accumulate a larger raw count for free, is 0.202 at 256 against 0.310 at 64 (64 worse by 0.115, 7W/3L, p = 0.344); topples are 0 at 256 against 0.27 per episode at 64; peak kinetic energy 10.19 against 17.87, though that mean is carried by one outlier episode at 123.0 and the sign test is 3W/7L. So 256 is if anything gentler on the shake, not harsher, and the earlier single-episode reading is withdrawn. The priority concern SURVIVES in direction and not in significance: priority_clean_ratio is 0.575 at 256 against 0.803 at 64 (6W/3L/1T, p = 0.508). soft_clean_ratio is unchanged (0.950 against 0.978, 1W/1L/8T). entries.claim: The two independently developed work-bound instruments are unified on POLICY_ATTEMPT_BUDGET; ONLINE_FIXED_WORK_ATTEMPTS and FIXED_WORK_DEADLINE_GUARD_SECONDS are REMOVED rather than left beside it as a second name for the same control. POLICY_ATTEMPT_BUDGET won because it also records the work the SHIPPED deadline path consumes (attempts_consumed, now written unconditionally), which is what a budget has to be calibrated from -- the removed implementation had no calibration and its budget was guessed. effective_attempt_budget() resolves the two ways a budget can arrive: an explicit caller argument wins, otherwise the constant applies, and 0 still means off. Without it the merge would have silently ignored the explicit budgets that scripts/measure_same_class_stacking.py passes to PlacementCore.choose, which is the entire basis of the fallback-is-search-allocation finding. This also closes an unexplained result on this branch. The base arm moved from 84 to 69 placed on the development suite between two sessions with an identical binary, which was recorded as unexplained. The cause is that the online search stops on a wall clock, so CPU speed decides how much anchor space fits in 6.5 s and therefore which trajectory an episode takes. Independently, trunk work found b000-k40 returning placed 11 / fill 14.059 identically at --parallel 3 and --parallel 1 against a committed guard of 21 / 29.220 -- deterministic slow-box behaviour, not scheduler noise -- and moved the regression guard to CI for that reason.

That is why the constant is calibrated from recorded attempts_consumed rather than chosen. It removes Var_xi given the arrival order and does not remove Var_omega, which is a property of the problem. It defines a MEASUREMENT policy: a fixed-work number is never shipped performance.

entries.claim: A forward-looking HANDOFF section written at the end of the branch named 'extend the offline objective from 2 of 6 components' as the largest Task A lever. An audit showed the premise is false and the recommended action would have been a no-op. OFFLINE_FILL_WEIGHT and OFFLINE_STABILITY_WEIGHT feed only DryRunResult.weighted_score() at agent/agent.py:941, which has no callers anywhere in the repository. Order selection is result.rank_key() > best_result.rank_key() at agent/agent.py:6350, a five-element LEXICOGRAPHIC tuple (placed_count, placed_volume, fill_ratio, stability_proxy, -normalized_center_of_mass_z). Sweeping the two weights 0.65/0.35 -> 0.0/1.0 -> 99.0/-99.0 leaves behaviour_sha256 bit-identical while component_sha256 moves, by the same fingerprint probe ADR-003 used for the risk-lambda gap. The tuple is narrower than five terms: fill_ratio is placed_volume over a case-fixed capacity, hence a monotone transform of placed_volume, so the effective key is (placed_count, placed_volume) and stability and cog are consulted only between orders placing the same items. The correct diagnosis is lexicographic domination by placed_count, and the work is replacing rank_key rather than tuning weights. Two further claims in that section were also wrong. Raising the offline budget is already measured and flat -- at OFFLINE_MAX_EVALUATIONS 50, 55, 60 and unlimited the search selects an identical 41-element order -- and 13381bd moved orders evaluated 3.0 -> 51.3 rather than being the state where only 3 were reachable. ADR-003 also constrains this area rather than leaving it open. Separately, the cause-of-death dichotomy claimed for the first-pass change does not survive. Over all 30 episodes of reports/first-pass-depth every arm ends is_placed_safe False 10 of 10; only the terminal fallback rate moves and it is non-monotonic (base 3/10, 128 6/10, 256 4/10), and the difference vanishes in reports/stability-tradeoff. The original claim read one 5-episode block.

entries.claim: Three of the four container-configuration axes the competition declares had never been executed, and building a probe for them immediately found a hard crash. COMPETITION_RULES section 2 states every task is posed with combinations of one or two containers, shelf present or absent, empty or pre-loaded, and a priority-dedicated container present or absent; the official QA additionally forbids per-task submissions, so one agent must self-detect the setup and these branches WILL be taken. The bundled sample_config.json covers exactly one axis: both cases are single-container, empty, no dedicated container, differing only in the shelf, and the whole development suite derives from those two cases by changing look-ahead, so it inherits the same blind spot. First defect found: a two-container config built by copying the bundled camera block raises IndexError in env.reset() at env.py:318, because camera.num_containers sizes the shared depth-map array (env.py:80-88) and the bundled value is 1. That is a config-side defect rather than a simulator bug, but it is unavoidable for anyone who has never built a two-container scene. With it corrected the dual-dedicated-priority scene RUNS: placed fraction 0.732 (30 of 41), is_valid true, container usage 22 on index 0 and 9 on index 1, priority_misrouted 0 -- so multi-container placement and dedicated routing both work in physics for the first time. Two caveats on that number: two containers give roughly twice the volume for the same 41-item mix, so 0.732 is not comparable to the single-container development suite or to the official 0.505; and priority_clean_ratio ends at 0.333, so priority items are being covered even though they are routed correctly. Still unmeasured: the 80-item two-container scale the rules describe for Task A.

PHYSICS_LATERAL_GUARD (the self-imposed 10 mm on top of the official 15 mm transport clearance) is a SETTLE-SURVIVAL margin, not a search restriction, and lowering it is a regression under the shipped policy. Six scenario-matrix scenes, shipped mode, same machine: 10 mm ends 3 completed / 3 pre-check deaths, 2 mm ends 0 completed / 4 PHYSICAL settle failures (is_valid true, is_placed_safe false) / 2 pre-check -- every episode 10 mm completed becomes a physical failure at 2 mm. Paired Task B CI on the same runner generation, 3 replicates per pool, gate off: pool 10 18.00->15.00, pool 20 19.33->13.33, pool 40 20.00->16.00 placed; suite 57.33->44.33, fill 70.05->54.94, within-arm replicate spread ~0. The effect is not mediated by search volume: under the deadline 2 mm reaches MORE attempts (4518 vs 3651 per step) and MORE accepted candidates (850 vs 565) and still loses. Default reverted to 0.010; the knob remains for further study.

A POLICY_ATTEMPT_BUDGET ablation can rank arms that the shipped policy ranks the other way, because the budget puts the agent in a different operating point. POLICY_ATTEMPT_BUDGET=4000 runs ~2500 attempts/step against ~3651 under the shipped deadline -- about 30% below -- and a starved search loses episodes to physical settle failures for reasons unrelated to the arm under test (the 10 mm guard dies physically in 4 of 6 matrix scenes at budget 4000, 0 of 6 under the deadline). Both arms consumed identical work there (2496 vs 2495 attempts/step), so it was a FAIR comparison of the WRONG regime. Separately, search breadth itself is not harmful: at a fixed guard, attempts/step 1739/2558/3411 give placed 110/164/172 with physical deaths 2/4/1, monotonically better, which REFUTES the intermediate claim that more candidates make this ranker worse. Rule: run contract ablations at or above the shipped attempt rate, or in shipped mode outright.

Priority items get covered by non-priority items through the RELEASE path, closing the HANDOFF thread that suspected it. Aligning per-step priority_covered_by_other increments with the policy trace across the dual scenario-matrix scenes: 6 of 7 cover events were release actions. Mechanism: release_rest_height() treats every packed top as a landing surface and release_rejection_reason() has no support check, so planning a rest on a priority top is legal. Release is not a corner case -- about half of all shipped-mode actions are release candidates. A hard reject (RELEASE_ATTRIBUTE_GUARD=all) cuts suite priority covers 7 -> 2 but costs 47 suite placed in pi_B; restricting it to priority tops only (mode 'priority') recovers about a third of that cost (164 vs 150 vs base 197 on the comparable 7-scene subset) because the shelf scenes' binding rejections ARE priority-top rests -- late-game survival was being bought by covering priority items. Default off; the recorded next shape is a lexicographic preference (avoid covering while a non-covering candidate exists) rather than a hard reject.

entries.claim: OFFICIAL RULING (SIGNATE, 2026-08-04): the shelf-height planes in PlacementValidator.check_transport_path()'s resting_surfaces and ceiling_surfaces apply REGARDLESS of require_shelf, and this is intended, not a defect. The stated reason is that require_shelf controls only the CENTRE shelf, while the left-ear small shelf always exists and divides the space, so the plane is a permanent structural constraint. resting_surfaces (thickness, height/2+thickness+buffer): a load bottom within 0-50 mm of either plane counts as a direct slide approach onto a shelf/frame top and gets NO extra lift (effective_start_z=0). ceiling_surfaces (height/2+buffer, height+buffer-thickness): the shelf underside also always acts as a clearance ceiling and clips the lift. Official advice when this causes an unwanted rejection: move the target Z by a few millimetres to leave the 0-50 mm band, or reorder the loading. DO NOT make these planes conditional; tests/test_transport_plane_contract.py pins it.
